questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** it depends on the boot. He says finished, pretreated leather doesn't need treating out of the box, but distressed leather like Rustic Brown is worth treating. As for frequency, by 2022 he had no fixed schedule and treated his boots when they looked or felt dry.

**Out of the box**
- He read Blundstone's FAQ, which says most of their boots come pretreated and that it does not recommend treating them out of the box. [1]
- The exception is distressed leathers (Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse, Rustic Black). The FAQ says you may treat these but don't have to, and that it will darken the leather. [2]
- For his own Rustic Brown pair, he recommends conditioning and doesn't recommend leaving them dry, even though that's the look people buy them for. [3]
- In his first review he said he'd treat his pair anyway, because he bought them assuming they were already treated. [4]

**How often**
- **Most recent (2022):** he says he doesn't know how often, and that he personally probably does too little. He treats his boots when he feels they need it, and says to go by intuition. [5]
- His signs that it's time are leather that looks or feels dry, or water no longer beading on top. In that case he says to add wax or oil. He also says to clean them regularly, because dirt wears the leather down faster. [6]
- **Earlier (2019):** he was stricter. He said you may have to wax them every month, or maybe every week if you're hard on them. [7] He also said to treat any leather you haven't conditioned in a few months. [3]

So his view loosened from a rough monthly routine to treating them as needed. He also says how much you wear them and where you go affects the timing. [5]

He has only talked about this for Blundstones. He hasn't covered other boot types here.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, the first soak or wash shrinks them, mainly in the waist, but he says they loosen again with wear.** Because of that shrinkage, his rule is to size up.

**Sizing (his latest view, 2025):** He says you should usually go two sizes up with the 501 STF, and that you put them in the bathtub to shrink them [1]. In 2023 he added that Levi's recommends two sizes up in the waist, and that the waist numbers don't follow vanity sizing, so the jeans shrink down [2].

**How much they shrink depends on your wash (2023):** His shrunk STFs ended up smaller than regular rinsed 501s [3]. He says that if you put them in the dryer or very hot water, they'd start out a lot smaller. He didn't use very hot water or the dryer, and his looked way better. His advice is not to toss them in the dryer or rinse them that hot, and you get a really nice fit [4]. He also bets that with frequent wear they'd stretch out to about the same size as the rinsed pair [5].

**What happened with his own pairs (2019–2020):**
- In 2019 he soaked them in hot water and found they definitely slimmed up, mostly in the waist, while the length barely changed [6]. He says he believes the shrinking really happens as they dry [7].
- A week later, the upper thigh and waist had stretched enough that he could wear a belt [8].
- In 2020 he had bought a 29 waist, ignoring Levi's advice, and could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe. He was glad he did, because after a year they were a really good fit for him [9]. He says he should have bought a 32 length, though [9].

**Not covered:** He doesn't say how much further they shrink in ordinary washes after the first soak.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
By his rule, a 33x30 would mean buying a **35x32** in the 501 STF. That is two sizes up in the waist and two inches more in length. He hasn't said anything about how 502 sizing compares to 501 sizing, so I'm applying his rule to the numbers you gave.

**His latest view (2025):** he says you should usually go two sizes up in the STF 501 [1]. His fuller version, from 2021, is that Levi's recommends two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer than you'd normally wear [2]. In 2023 he explained why: the STF's labeled waist is much larger than the finished jeans, because they shrink down [3].

**He didn't always follow this.** In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a smaller waist because jeans are usually too long on him [4]. A year later he said he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe, though the fit was good once they loosened. He also said he would have gotten a 32 length [5]. By 2021 he said Levi's is correct, and that it took him four pairs of 501s to realize it [2].

**Caveats:**
- He says a 36 waist may not exist, so check that your size is actually available [6].
- To get a good fit, he says not to use very hot water or the dryer [7].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He mostly cuffs for fit and style, mainly to deal with length and wide legs, though he has said he now likes jeans over boots more than cuffs.

**Most recent (2020, Levi's 501 one-year update):** He cuffed his 501s because he doesn't think his current style suits uncuffed wider-legged pants [1]. He also says he should have bought a 32 length, so the cuff partly covers jeans that came out short [1].

**Earlier (2019, Levi's 501 shrink-to-fit video):** For him it comes down to length. If jeans look too long, they just look bad, and that's the first thing he cares about [2]. He also says the cuff can't be too thick [2].

**A shift with boots (late 2019, L.L. Bean boots):** He says he always used to cuff his jeans, but now likes them down over his boots a little more [3]. He says this calms the boots down as a loud fashion piece [3].

**Newer approach to length (2025):** He doesn't talk about cuffing here. He buys jeans about 3.5–4% longer to allow for shrinkage, then has them hemmed if they're still too long after a few washes [4].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, though he's hedged since.** In 2022 he called the 3335s his favorite boots ever and said they beat the 1907s. By September 2023 he said the 3335s "still might be" his favorite Red Wings, but probably not, and he was selling them.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):** He's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time. He hedges that: "they still might be but they probably not the 875s the 1907s the iron Rangers all have their own characteristics" he really likes [1]. He still likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, light weight and nimble feel, and says they're easier for walking or a light hike. He adds that "they're going", meaning he's selling them [2].

**Earlier view (Oct 2022):** This was a clear yes. He said the 3335s are his favorite boots he's ever had, and that they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [3]. His reasoning:
- He's hiking and walking in the woods rather than doing heritage work, so he calls them "a dramatically better all-around boot" [3].
- He prefers their Vibram mini lug sole to the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s, which he thinks will break down faster [4].
- The caveat: the 1907s and 875s are more beefily built, so if you need a tough boot, the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [3].

**Before that (Sept 2021):** He was strongly pro-1907. He said that if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing, you should get the 1907s [5]. He also said he doesn't really like crepe soles [5].

He hasn't said in the videos available here that he's switched back to the 1907s.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of late 2023 he's still a big fan of Blundstones, but he's retiring his heavily worn pair of 585s as part of cutting down his boot collection. It's a culling decision, not a change of heart.

**Latest view (Sept 2023):** He says his 585s, the subject of his very first video, have held up and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" despite constant wear [1]. He's "a big fan" and says he's "always loved them" [1], and that they hold a special place in his heart [2]. Even so, he says it's "time to retire those bunnies" [3].

**Slip-on convenience:** He likes boots he can flop on quickly for errands or rain, lumping them in with Blundstones as shoes that work in any weather [4]. He says he's keeping that slip-on pair but could easily put it on the sell list [4]. It's not fully clear from his wording which pair that refers to.

**How his view got here:**
- 2019: He recommended them "100%" if you'll keep them treated, and called them his favorites of the boots he owned [5][6].
- 2020: After a year he said "still great boots" [7].
- 2022: He said they're worth the hype ("I think so!") and still among his favorites, though not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [8].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He says Solovair is the better buy, and that Made in England Dr. Martens are mainly for big fans of the brand. He compared them directly in 2022. Later videos add a caveat about Solovair's quality control but don't reverse his view.

**Direct comparison (2022):**
- He says the Made in England Docs have better leather and midsoles, but he rates both as probably on par with Solovair. [1]
- He thinks the extra price of the England Docs is mostly for the "made in England" part, and says Solovairs are actually cheaper. [2]
- For Solovair he lists a shank that makes them more comfortable over long periods, and more conventional Goodyear welting that makes them easier to resole. [3]
- He calls the Solovair Derby eight-eye essentially the same boot as the Docs, from the original maker. [3]
- The one thing Solovair lacks is the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs. [4]

**Caveat on Solovair:**
- Even in 2022 he mentioned a defect on his own pair, a ripped back tab and a snapped lace, which he assumed was a manufacturing defect. [5]
- In September 2023 he recapped that quality-control problem and said Solovair's response was to send the wrong parts and tell him to repair it himself. [6]
- He still says he really likes the boots, though they feel too roomy on his feet, which he thinks probably means he sized wrong. [7]
- He would sell his pair only to buy another pair of monkey boots. [7]

**Made in England on its own (2023):**
- Compared with the cheaper Thailand 1460, he says the England pair is probably not worth the extra $90 from a purely robotic standpoint. [8]
- He says you have to be a mega fan to get them. [9]

He didn't directly compare the two again after the 2022 video.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hiking in Blundstones, but his comments lean toward them not being the ideal boot for a 4-day hike. He sees them as a casual, walking-around boot rather than a serious hiking boot.

**What he's said about hiking in them**
- In his one-year review (2020), he says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. He still took them up and down a few mountains in Maine, and they "held up well" even though they got scuffed [2].
- He calls them "decent for work boots but not anything incredible" [3]. He describes them as a good balance for going out for a walk around a city or town [4].
- In his first review (2019), he said the boots "can kind of go anywhere", and that includes hiking [5]. He also found them comfortable but "nothing super super crazy" [6].

**Things to watch for**
- **Break-in:** After a year, he got "big fat gross blisters" when he started running and walking the track in them, which stopped after two to three weeks [7]. For a 4-day hike, that suggests not wearing a pair that isn't broken in.
- **Water:** They're water resistant, not waterproof. He says you can get them wet, "but don't go swimming in them because water's gonna come in" [8]. He says his own pair stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" over time [9].

**What he reaches for on longer hikes**
He describes the Hoka Kaha GTX as "essentially computers for your feet", his first modern hiking boots [10]. He praises the Jim Green Razorbacks for their padding, saying "if you're going hiking for a long time that's good stuff" [11].

He hasn't given a verdict on Blundstones for several days in a row, so these are the closest things he's said.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
For the best price-to-quality, he points to the Uniqlo tee, and for someone taller or wider he suggests Muji instead. He hasn't said what size he'd pick for a 5'11", 225 lb build, so the size advice below is only his general rules applied to you.

**His newest verdict (Sept 2025)**
- He calls the $20 Uniqlo tee "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1].
- He says that unless you're taller or wider, Uniqlo is the one, and that if you are, "you'd want Muji" [2]. It costs about $4–5 more, but it is "significantly longer and a good deal wider" [2]. With your build, his rule points to Muji.
- In June 2025 he said of Uniqlo that for $15 "they're very very good" and that you get a bound neck collar so it doesn't wiggle [3]. He also said Muji feels justified at about $10 more, with a thicker, tighter collar [3].

**Other value picks he likes**
- **Bronson (about $29):** He says it is a very good shirt for the price [4]. He says Bronson and Bravestar are probably neck and neck for the greatest value, slightly above Uniqlo [4].
- **House of Blanks ($35, made in Canada):** He says it has zero torque and is "truly an outstanding value" [5].
- **Los Angeles Apparel:** He says that if you size down one, it might win [6].
- **Kirkland six-pack (2024):** About $4.20 a shirt. He calls it fantastic and "quite long" [7].

**Size**
He hasn't given a size for your height and weight. His only sizing guidance for you is to go to Muji for extra length and width, and to size down one in the LA Apparel [2][6]. Check the length and width measurements for Muji against your own.

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't name one winner, and his newest t-shirt video says why: the best tee depends on your preferences. If you want a short list from his own picks, he points to **Uniqlo** as the cheap pick, **Front General Store** as the nicer budget pick, and **Bronson** for value.

**Short list from his picks**
- **Uniqlo ($20):** He calls it "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [2]. If you're taller or wider, he says you'd want Muji instead [3].
- **Front General Store ($40, made in Japan):** Choosing between it and House of Blanks, he says "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [4]. It's the pick if you want more character; House of Blanks is the pick if you want perfectly smooth with no torque [4].
- **Bronson (about $29):** He left it out of the big video but notes why it "usually wins or comes close" [5]. In mid-2025 he said he'd give the win to Bronson's standard loopwheel tubular tee over the Bravestar tee [6].

- **All-arounder:** J Press x American Trench [7].
- **Japanese:** Wonder Looper, for the fit [8].
- **Heavyweight:** American Giant, "by a long shot" [9].
- **Elevated and minimalist:** Merz b. Schwanen's 2M15, though he says Lady White could just as well be his favorite and "they're all great choices" [10].

**Earlier note:** In 2024 he named Asket the overall winner of that year's roundup [11].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** He sees the 1907 as the 875 plus a storm welt and a couple of extras for about $10 more. In 2021 he called the 1907 the best Red Wing moc toe. By 2023 he is softer, saying the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes. He also says the 3335 is his favourite Red Wing of all time, though "they still might be" is hedged.

**His view over time**
- 2021: he says the 1907s are in his opinion Red Wing's best heritage boots "by far" and that you should get them if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing. [1]
- 2023: he says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics that I really really like". [2]

**Construction**
- 875: he says it is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant, and says the welt leaves room for cork that molds to your foot. [3]
- 1907: it has a storm (Norwegian-like) welt. He relays the popular Reddit view that Red Wing just stitches another strip of leather onto the welt, but adds "i'm not quite sure". [4] To him the storm welt is "invaluable". [5]

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875. [6]
- For that he says you get a removable leather footbed, which he says is normally about $40 separately, plus leather laces, which he says are typically $15. [5]
- He also says the footbed can be pulled out to help the boots dry. [5]

**What they share**
- In 2022 he groups them together: both have crepe soles, which he thinks break down faster than the 3335's Vibram sole. [7] He had also said in 2021 that he doesn't really like crepe soles. [1]
- In 2022 he calls both "more beefily constructed" than the 3335. He says that if you need a tough boot, they are the ones to go for over the 3335. [8]

**Water performance (1907 only)**
In his waterproof test, the right 1907 leaked almost immediately through stitching, which he called a letdown. He still has no doubt they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud. [9] He hasn't tested the 875 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
There's no single winner, but by his latest word (Sept 2025) Uniqlo is the best value, and the Front General Store is the one he'd rather wear if you can spend about $40.

**Uniqlo (~$15-20):** In 2025 he calls the $20 tee "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He describes it as a rough, open-end "starter t-shirt" [2], and says the $15 price and bound collar are very good [5]. In 2024 he named the Uniqlo heavyweight crew the best value heavyweight or all-around tee [9]. He also said it "may be" the best bargain tee [10].

**Front General Store ($38-40):** He says it's a step up in feel and character. He calls it "a $40 100% made in Japan shirt. Great proportions, great feel" [3]. In June 2025 he called it "still really good" [6]. In Sept 2025, picking between it and House of Blanks for the budget category, he said "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [4]. In 2024 he said it was "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want an upgrade under $40 [7], with a softness of 6/10 [7].

**Pro Club:** He liked it ("I really like proc Club") but found it the roughest shirt in that video, with a softness of 4/10 [8].

**Hanes:** He calls it "your classic $10 great shirt" with a softness of 7/10 [11]. Separately, he says the ultra-cheap mass-market brands rush production, and that all five shirts he had from those brands had a defect [12]. He lumps "Hannes and Gild" together in that group [13].

**Bottom line:** Uniqlo is the best value per dollar. Front General Store is the pick if you want more character and can pay about double. Pro Club and Hanes are cheap, solid classics. He hasn't compared Uniqlo directly against Pro Club or Hanes in a single ranking.

The Iron Snail hasn't compared the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker with a specific rival for rain, wind and spring use, and I can't tell which jacket "this" refers to. questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't address that directly in the videos available here. In 2023 he reviewed an unlined Huckberry waxed trucker and called the lack of a lining its con. By 2025 he describes the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as lined and mentions a wool-lined version, so your point matches how he talks about it now.

**2023 (Waxed Jacket Olympics):** He called the Huckberry jacket "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1]. His con was a personal preference: he always likes a lining on waxed jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms. He said Huckberry and Rogue Territory share this con [2]. He never mentions a flannel-lined version in that video.

**2025 (Internet's Favorite Waxed Jackets):** In a Huckberry-sponsored segment, he says the Flint and Tinder trucker is lined, so it's comfortable and you don't get wax on your skin [3]. He also says they make a wool-lined one that he's yet to get [4]. He did say he talked about this jacket many times before being sponsored [5]. Treat his praise there with the sponsorship in mind.

**His broader view of lining:** He still says he usually wants a liner on waxed jackets because the wax gets on your skin [6]. But he adds that in his old age he sees why you wouldn't line something, since satin sleeves limit how often you can wear the jacket [7].

So the con in 2023 applied to the specific unlined jacket he was reviewing, and he has since hedged on how much unlined matters. He hasn't said why he didn't factor in the lined versions in 2023.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s with the 875s in the videos available here. He does describe how the 3335s fit, and says a little about the 875s' build.

**3335 fit:** He went true to size and says they fit fine [1]. He notes the profile is very slim because the outsole is very thin, and the boots taper down [1]. With thin cotton socks in warm weather he had no tightness. With wool socks his toes feel squished and he can't wiggle them much [1].

**875 build, for contrast:** He says the 875s and 1907s are more beefily constructed than the 3335s [2]. That is about construction, not a sizing comparison.
